message.content:
Below is a **sample 7‑day “Paris in a Week” itinerary** that balances the classic sights with some lesser‑known gems, plus practical tips on how to get around, where to stay, what to eat, and how to keep costs reasonable.  
Feel free to tweak the days, swap activities, or extend the trip—Paris is a city that rewards exploration.

---

## 1️⃣ Pre‑Trip Checklist

| Item | Why It Matters | Suggested Resources |
|------|----------------|---------------------|
| **Passport & Visa** | Check expiration (must be valid for at least 6 months). U.S., Canada, EU, Australia, New Zealand, and many others have visa‑free entry for 90 days. | [EU Visa Info](https://ec.europa.eu/visa/) |
| **Travel Insurance** | Covers medical emergencies, trip cancellations, lost luggage. | Allianz Travel, World Nomads, Travel Guard |
| **Currency** | Euro (€). Bring a mix of cash and a card that offers no foreign‑transaction fees. | Revolut, Wise, or a credit card with no foreign fees |
| **SIM / Roaming** | Free data via Wi‑Fi in most cafés; consider a local SIM for navigation. | Orange, SFR, Bouygues Telecom |
| **Packing List** | Light, versatile clothing, comfortable shoes, power adapter (Type C/F). | PackPoint app |
| **Flight Booking** | Book 2–3 months ahead for best fares. | Google Flights, Skyscanner, Momondo |
| **Accommodation Booking** | Book 4–6 weeks in advance for best rates. | Booking.com, Airbnb, Hostelworld |
| **Transport Pass** | A 10‑ride carnet or a 7‑day Navigo pass saves money on Metro/RER. | [Navigo Pass](https://www.ratp.fr/en/navigo) |
| **City Pass** | Optional: Paris Pass (museum access + hop‑on bus). | [Paris Pass](https://www.parispass.com) |

---

## 2️⃣ Accommodation Options

| Budget | Recommendation | Why |
|--------|----------------|-----|
| **$30–$70/night** | **Hostel** – Generator Paris (Le Marais), St Christopher’s Inn (Montmartre) | Social atmosphere, free breakfast |
| **$80–$150/night** | **Mid‑range Hotel** – Hotel Ekta (Champs‑Élysées), Hotel de la Porte Dorée (Bastille) | Comfortable, central |
| **$200+** | **Luxury** – Hôtel Plaza Athénée (Avenue Montaigne), Le Meurice (Place de la Concorde) | Iconic, top service |

*Tip:* Staying in **Le Marais** or **Saint‑Germain‑en‑Laye** gives you easy access to the city center while offering a quieter vibe.

---

## 3️⃣ Transportation in Paris

| Mode | How to Use | Cost (approx.) |
|------|------------|----------------|
| **Metro** | 2‑hour single ticket €1.90, 10‑ride carnet €14.90 | €1.90 per ride |
| **RER** | Regional trains to suburbs (Versailles, Disneyland) | €2.40–€5.00 |
| **Bus** | 2‑hour single ticket €1.90 | €1.90 |
| **Bike (Vélib’)** | 30‑min pass €5.90, 1‑day pass €12.90 | €5.90 |
| **Taxi / Ride‑share** | Uber, Bolt | €15–€25 for city rides |
| **Walking** | Most attractions are within walking distance | Free |

*Tip:* Buy a **Navigo Week Pass** (€22.80) for unlimited travel on Metro, RER, buses, trams, and the RER B to Charles de Gaulle Airport.

---

## 4️⃣ 7‑Day Itinerary

> **Assumption:** You arrive on Day 1 morning and depart on Day 7 evening. Adjust times based on your flight schedule.

### Day 1 – Arrival & Settling In
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Arrive at Charles de Gaulle or Orly. Take RER B to your hotel. |
| **Afternoon** | Explore the neighborhood (Le Marais or Saint‑Germain). Grab lunch at a local café. |
| **Evening** | Dinner at **Le Petit Cler** (french bistro). Walk along the Seine, cross Pont Neuf. |

### Day 2 – Classic Icons
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Eiffel Tower (buy tickets online to skip lines). |
| **Afternoon** | Picnic in Champ de Mars. Visit Musée d’Orsay (pre‑book tickets). |
| **Evening** | Seine river cruise (Bateaux Mouches) – sunset view. |

### Day 3 – Louvre & Palais Royal
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Louvre Museum (early opening, 9 am). |
| **Afternoon** | Walk through Palais Royal gardens, shop at boutiques. |
| **Evening** | Dinner in the 1st arrondissement (e.g., **Café Marly**). |

### Day 4 – Montmartre & Sacré‑Coeur
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Climb to Sacré‑Coeur, enjoy panoramic views. |
| **Afternoon** | Explore Place du Tertre, visit the Salvador Dalí Museum. |
| **Evening** | Cabaret show at Moulin Rouge (optional). |

### Day 5 – Day Trip to Versailles
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | RER C to Versailles Château. |
| **Afternoon** | Tour the palace, stroll the Hall of Mirrors, explore the gardens. |
| **Evening** | Return to Paris, dinner at **Le Relais de l’Entrecôte** (steak & fries). |

### Day 6 – Hidden Gems & Shopping
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Canal Saint‑Martin walk, brunch at **Café Pinson**. |
| **Afternoon** | Visit the **Musée Rodin** or **Musée de l’Orangerie** (for Monet). |
| **Evening** | Shopping in the Marais (boutiques, vintage shops). |

### Day 7 – Last‑Minute Culture & Departure
| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| **Morning** | Visit the **Centre Pompidou** (modern art). |
| **Afternoon** | Quick stop at **Pont Alexandre III** for photos. |
| **Evening** | Head to the airport via RER B or taxi. |

---

## 5️⃣ Dining Highlights

| Dish | Where |
|------|-------|
| Croissants & Café au lait | **Du Pain et des Idées** (Canal Saint‑Martin) |
| Escargot | **L’Arpège** (3‑star Michelin) |
| Crêpes | **Crêperie Bretonne** (Montparnasse) |
| French Onion Soup | **Le Comptoir du Relais** (Saint‑Germain) |
| Cheese & Wine | **Fromagerie Barthélemy** (Le Marais) |
| Street Food | **L’As du Fallafel** (Le Marais) |

*Tip:* Try a **bistro lunch** (mid‑price, hearty) for a quick, authentic experience.

---

## 6️⃣ Budget Estimate (per person)

| Category | Approx. Cost |
|----------|--------------|
| Flights (round‑trip) | $400–$800 |
| Accommodation (7 nights) | $350–$1,200 |
| Transport Pass | €22.80 (~$25) |
| Food & Drink | $300–$500 |
| Attractions (tickets) | $150–$250 |
| Miscellaneous (souvenirs, tips) | $100–$200 |
| **Total** | **$1,300–$3,000** |

*(Prices vary by season, booking time, and personal spending habits.)*

---

## 7️⃣ Packing Essentials

| Item | Why |
|------|-----|
| Comfortable walking shoes | 20+ hours of walking |
| Light jacket & umbrella | Weather can be unpredictable |
| Power adapter (Type C/F) | For charging devices |
| Reusable water bottle | Stay hydrated |
| Small backpack | Carry essentials during day trips |
| Travel guidebook or offline map | Navigation without data |
| Copies of passport & travel documents | Safety |

---

## 8️⃣ Quick Tips & Hacks

1. **Book museum tickets online** – skip the long queues.  
2. **Use the “Paris Pass”** if you plan to visit many museums; it includes a hop‑on bus.  
3. **Eat lunch at a boulangerie** – cheaper than restaurants.  
4. **Take advantage of free museum days** (first Sunday of the month, 2nd Sunday of the month for certain museums).  
5. **Walk between attractions** – Paris is very walkable; you’ll discover hidden cafés.  
6. **Avoid tourist traps** – stay away from souvenir stalls near major landmarks.  
7. **Learn basic French phrases** – locals appreciate the effort.  
8. **Check the weather forecast** – Paris can rain unexpectedly.  

---

## 9️⃣ Final Thoughts

Paris is a city that blends history, art, cuisine, and romance. With this itinerary, you’ll see the iconic sights, taste authentic French fare, and experience the city’s vibrant neighborhoods—all while staying mindful of your budget.  

Enjoy your trip! Bon voyage!
